To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
irrigation with saline drainage water of varying ec values (6, 9 or 12 dS / m) did not cause any soil degradation and did not adversely affect wheat grain yield and protein content.

irrigation of wheat crop with drainage water of high salinity ( ec > 18–27dS/m) is detrimental to crop yield and soil salinity build up, while use of drainage water of lower salinity ( ec < 18–27ds/m) is not.

wheat can be irrigated with drainage water without any significant reduction in yield provided that the water is used in diluted form and that the drainage water is applied during the early growth stages of wheat.

a case study of a field experiment in which drainage water of different levels of salinity was used for irrigation of wheat on a sandy loom soil.
the use of saline drainage water of varying quality for irrigation of wheat in a sandy loam.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
irrigation with diluted drainage water at a salinity level of up to 12 dS / m does not affect the growth and yield of winter wheat.
irrigation with saline drainage water of ec = 6,12 and 18 dS/m can be used without dilution to irrigate wheat on a sandy loamy soil without causing yield losses.
irrigation with saline drainage water of up to 18–27dS/m is feasible and safe for wheat production on a sandy loams soil.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
irrigation of wheat with saline ( ec > 6 dS/m) drainage water on a coarse-textured soil is feasible without causing any serious problems of soil degradation.
irrigation of wheat with diluted drainage water up to 12 dS / m does not pose any serious problem of soil degradation and yield loss, and can be used for irrigation in a rotation of rice–wheat.
the use of saline drainage water for irrigation, after appropriate dilution, can be a useful option for irrigation in the command area of a drainage project.

drainage water with an ec as high as 27 dS/m can be safely used for wheat irrigation, provided that it is used without dilution, and if the drainage water is not used for irrigation, it can be safely disposed of by deep percolation.
